item.title: Building the Fundraising Engine
item.description:
Talk Summary

Building the fundraising engine for the GNOME Foundation — exploring how community-driven organizations can build sustainable funding through campaigns, donor relations, and community engagement.

Topics Discussed

  • Sustainable fundraising strategies for open source foundations
  • Community engagement as a driver of donations
  • Donor relations and long-term financial health
  • The role of the board in organizational sustainability

Notes

Delivered at GUADEC 2026, the GNOME project’s annual conference.

item.title: Tux Digital Podcast — Linux App Summit
item.description:
Talk Summary

Podcast-style conversation with Michael Tunnell on the Tux Digital show, joined by Aleix Pol, discussing Linux App Summit — the conference, the app ecosystem, and the future of Linux applications. Approximately 90 minutes with ~8k views.

Topics Discussed

  • Linux App Summit and the Linux app ecosystem
  • Flatpak and direct app delivery
  • GNOME and KDE collaboration
  • The future of Linux applications

Notes

The exposure helped drive awareness and attendance for LAS 2026.

item.title: Applying balm on dev burnout through community
item.description:
Abstract

Exploring the latest developments in AI-powered development tools and their impact on developer workflows, from code completion to automated testing.

Key Points

  • Community can provide scalability if we include them by creating assets in documentation and code samples.
  • Creating a library of code samples will allow AI to automatically be trained on it. With coding AI agents becoming popular we can provide them with training material for more accurate results.

Notes

The talk was well received.

item.title: Using LLMs to Lower Barriers to Write Apps
item.description:
Talk Summary

Using LLMs to lower barriers to writing apps — exploring how large language models make app development more accessible, presented at Linux App Summit 2025 (which I also organized).

Topics Discussed

  • LLMs and app development accessibility
  • Lowering the barrier for new app developers
  • AI-assisted development workflows

item.title: oneAPI Meetup: Rusticl with Karol Herbst
item.description:
About This Meetup

The oneAPI Meetup Series was a community interview program hosted at Intel, bringing together developers, maintainers, and industry leaders to discuss the open source and heterogeneous computing ecosystem. Each episode featured a conversation with a key figure from the community — from kernel developers to compiler engineers to CEO-level leadership.

This episode features Karol Herbst on Rusticl — the Rust-based OpenCL implementation for Mesa — discussing its role in the open source GPU driver ecosystem and the future of portable compute.

item.title: The Mono Lake Story — How the Circular Economy Enables Open Hardware
item.description:
Talk Summary

The Mono Lake story — exploring how the circular economy enables open hardware. Drawing on the Mono Lake metaphor, the talk examines sustainable hardware models, refurbishment, and how circular approaches make open hardware ecosystems viable.

Topics Discussed

  • The circular economy and sustainable hardware
  • Open hardware ecosystems and their economic viability
  • Refurbishment and extended hardware lifecycles
  • How circular models enable broader access to hardware

Notes

From the professional career span — delivered during the ITRenew era, connecting sustainability with open hardware.
